Troops that would desert cannot be recruited from prisoners, notables' volunteers or by garrison auto-recruit (tavern mercenaries are not checked). With Recruitment Alignment on and its 'Only Good Rejects Evil' on, Evil lords and their garrisons shed no Free troops. When off, vanilla. This is the default for new campaigns. With the Alignment rules start option on Standard, a campaign follows this switch live; Strict or Relaxed fixes all four alignment switches for that campaign. Older saves follow this setting.
Fraction of each opposed-alignment troop type that deserts per day (minimum 1 per type). Default 0.50 = half per day. Higher clears mixed parties/garrisons faster.
When ON (default), YOUR party and garrisons shed opposed-alignment troops. When OFF, you may keep mixed-alignment troops (AI is still affected if 'Apply To AI Lords' is on).
When ON (default), AI lords' parties and garrisons also shed opposed-alignment troops. When OFF, only the player is affected (if 'Apply To Player' is on).
When ON (default), lords' field parties (including army members) shed opposed troops. When OFF, only garrisons are affected (if 'Apply To Garrisons' is on).
When ON (default), settlement garrisons shed opposed troops (e.g. a conquered fief's old-culture defenders leave). When OFF, only mobile parties are affected (if 'Apply To Mobile Parties' is on).

When enabled, an AI lord party whose clan is at its party limit takes one idle adult clan member along and gives that member a party role (scout, surgeon, engineer or quartermaster) the member is better at than the lord. The heroes go back to a settlement when the clan drops below its party limit or when this is turned off. When off, no new heroes join. A party whose disband starts always frees every hero aboard but its leader, with this on or off.

How many extra clan heroes one AI lord party may carry. Default 1. Heroes already riding along stay when you lower this. A hero who rides along costs the clan a daily wage and a party slot, and can be wounded, captured or killed in battle with the lord.

Master toggle for the combat feel pack: skill-based crush-through, monster/orc crush-through, creature cleave, creature stagger immunity, weight-based charge knockdown, shield penetration, race combat modifiers. When off, everything below is inert and combat behaves exactly as before this feature.

High-energy swings from an attacker who greatly outskills the defender have a chance to crush through the block (chance grows with skill gap and swing momentum; off-angle swings are penalized). Tuning constants live in combat_mechanics_config.json.
Troll, mumakil, war elephant and giant spider melee attacks can only be blocked with a SHIELD — a bare-weapon block is crushed through automatically.
AI orc/uruk swings can crush through even SHIELD blocks (energy- and skill-gated) — turtling against an orc horde is no longer safe. Never applies to the player's own attacks.

Troll and mumakil swings slice through a victim and carry 30% momentum into the next — one swing can hit multiple soldiers, including through shield blocks that take damage (a zero-damage block still stops the swing).
Big creatures shrug off hits below a per-creature damage threshold — no flinch-locking a troll with arrows. Thresholds live in combat_mechanics_config.json.

Mount charges knock down based on relative weight (charger + rider vs victim), charge speed and the victim's race resistance: a mumakil bowls over infantry, a horse can't floor a troll, dwarves stand their ground.

Missiles from config-listed weapon classes/items can penetrate shields and damage the soldier behind. Off by default, and the shipped lists are empty, so javelins behave as in the base game: only a HERO with the Throwing Impale perk pierces a shield. Regular troops never do, in vanilla or here. Turning this on with an empty config changes nothing; add entries in combat_mechanics_config.json first.

Per-race combat flavor from combat_mechanics_config.json: dwarves resist knockdown and stagger, elves crush through better and strike true from any angle, orcs swing with brute momentum. When off, all races use neutral values.
Ceiling for the skill-based crush-through chance, reached at a huge skill gap with a full-momentum swing. Default 50%.

Charger-to-victim weight ratio at which a charge ALWAYS knocks the victim down, from any angle, regardless of resistance (mumakil vs man is ~125, warg + orc vs man 8, horse + man vs man exactly 6). Default 6 since 2026-09-17, so a full-speed horse contact floors a man; raise it to 7 or 8 to give that back to wargs and chariots only. Values below the neutral weight ratio are treated as the neutral ratio. Saved values from before November 2026 were reset to this default; if you had chosen your own, set it again.

Charger-to-victim weight ratio at which a charge knocks down exactly as vanilla does (needs about 8 damage on a head-on hit). Heavier chargers than this ratio get MORE penetration, lighter ones less, down to the min factor. Default 6 = horse + man vs man. Lower it and every charge hits harder; raise it and only the heavy mounts do.

The base knockdown penetration of a charge at the neutral ratio and full speed. Default 0.4, vanilla's value, which cancels a troop's 0.4 base resistance so only Athletics protects him. 0.5 and up floors an ordinary man on any head-on hit that does damage; 0.3 needs a hard hit.

How far below vanilla the weight term may push a light charger's penetration against a heavy victim. Default 1.0 = never below vanilla (uruks and trolls fall like men; the troll, dwarf and Sauron race rows do the resisting). 0.25 restores the pre-2026-09-17 feel where a horse could not floor anything heavier than a man. The ceiling is the JSON's maxPenetrationFactor (shipped 2.5); a slider value above it is treated as that maximum.

Cavalry charge damage scales by the rider's culture (elves 1.6x, Rohan 1.5x, Rhun 1.4x, Gondor 1.3x, Dale and the orc kingdoms 1.2x, Erebor 1.0x). The table lives in combat_mechanics_config.json; this switch turns the whole thing off.

Configured heroes (shipped: Sauron and the Nine) get direction-mapped effects on any melee hit. Sauron: an overhead is a Slam (the struck foe always goes down, enemies in a ring around the impact are knocked down and take part of the damage, a burst of fear drains their morale; also fires on an overhead into the ground), a side swing is a Sweep (the struck foe and enemies in front are staggered back). The Nine: an overhead or a side swing is a Scream (enemies around the wraith take part of the damage, are staggered back and lose morale; the struck foe is staggered and frightened too). Never on a throw, a shot, a kick or bare hands. The same rules apply in a Custom Battle. Cooldowns and radii live in signature_strikes_config.json.

Multiplies every signature-strike cooldown (shipped: Sauron's Slam 20 s and Sweep 12 s, the Nine's Scream 15 s). Raise it if Sauron or the Nazgul feel overpowered; the JSON values need a full restart, this slider applies live.

A shield bash or a kick can floor a man. The chance grows with the attacker's Athletics lead over the victim; the victim's race and any race ability that toughens him cut it, a kick is weaker than a bash, and you resist more than a soldier does. Fighters who shrug off blows never fall: trolls while Creature Stagger Immunity is on, a soldier with a live race ability that shrugs off blows, and a hero with a career shrug-off passive. The numbers live in combat_mechanics_config.json.

Nazgul and Sauron drain the morale of enemy troops right beside them. The aura weakens them so they break sooner in the fighting, but it never routs anyone by itself. Takes effect immediately, but morale already drained is not restored when you switch it off.

Metres over which a wraith projects dread. Full strength within the inner radius from dread_aura_config.json (default 2m), falling to nothing at this distance. Default 5. The ceiling is 15: beyond 15 m the engine's proximity search stops using its grid and checks every agent on the field, on every pulse.

Morale per second drained at full strength, before the target's tier/hero resistance and its racial resistance. The aura stops at a morale floor of 10 (dread_aura_config.json), so it never routs anyone by itself. At the default 5.0, in an even fight, a tier-3 human reaches the floor after about 22 seconds of contact, a tier-6 elite about 37, and an elven hero of level 16 or more never. Below about 1.0 the engine's own morale recovery outpaces the drain.

When off, your team is immune and dread only touches the AI. Left on, an enemy wraith weakens your soldiers so they rout sooner in combat, and routed troops are LOST from your party. Your own character is always immune either way: the engine gives player-controlled agents no morale component at all.

AI soldiers fight with a battle ability for their race (or, for men, their culture) on a cooldown, fired when the moment comes and joined by nearby kin: berserkers go berserk when hurt in melee, Uruk-hai fall into bloodlust on a kill, dwarves stand fast against a charge or a crowd, elves quicken, orcs swarm, Rohan's riders spur on, Gondor closes ranks, and more. Your own character never fires one. Switching it on takes effect from the next battle; switching it off stops new abilities at once and lets running ones finish. Numbers live in race_abilities.json; the console command taom.print_race_abilities shows what each ability has done in the battle on screen.
The soldier who fires an ability, and a few of the kin who join him, shout in their own voice.
One line in the message log when five or more soldiers on either side fire the same ability within two seconds. Never one line per soldier.

Writes one log line for every wave of abilities and every phase change (active, spent, ready). Off, the log still gets a summary every 30 s of activity and at the end of each battle. For checking that the abilities work; leave off in normal play.

A soldier whose ability is active wears a coloured outline: red for fury, steel blue for a guard, violet for dread; the speed and aim abilities stay unlit. Sparks burst on the soldier who fires and on a few of the kin who join him. Only the soldiers nearest the camera are outlined (visuals.maxGlowing in race_abilities.json). Drawn on this client only, and hidden while Hide Battle UI is on.
Sauron and the Nazgûl Cannot Be Captured

When you beat them, they escape the field as fugitives instead of going to your dungeon, and return with a new army within days. This does NOT make them immortal: one of the Nine can still die in a battle he could not be captured in. Edit uncapturable_heroes_config.json to change who this covers.
Fade settlement nameplates with camera distance. When off, all nameplates display at full visibility regardless of distance (vanilla).
Camera distance at which fade begins. Nameplates closer than this stay fully opaque. Default 80.
Camera distance at which fade completes. Nameplates farther than this are fully hidden. Must be greater than Fade Start Distance. Default 200.

Tint each settlement plate by your relation to its owner: green for your own faction, red for an enemy, blue for an allied kingdom, plain parchment for neutral. Off leaves every plate parchment. Applies immediately.
How strongly the relation colour is applied to the bar, the name and the diamond frame. 100 is the full palette, 0 is plain parchment for everyone. Applies immediately. Default 100.
Opacity of a neutral settlement's plate. Vanilla uses 35, which can be faint over dark terrain. Tracked settlements keep vanilla's 80. Applies immediately. Default 35.

Opacity of a plate owned by your own faction, an enemy or an allied kingdom. Vanilla uses 50 for your own faction and 35 for the others. Tracked settlements keep vanilla's 80. Applies immediately. Default 50.

Size of party-icon figures and their mounts on the campaign map. Vanilla = 0.30; default 0.15 = half (makes parties feel smaller relative to settlements). Applies on the next icon rebuild after changing.

Another party's troop count on the campaign map blurs with its distance from you: '1??', '12?', then exact as you close in, and '...' at the very edge of sight. Standing closer, a higher Scouting skill and hosts of your own realm all sharpen it. Wounded and prisoner counts show only when the count is exact. A count you read stays remembered with a '~' and fades by the hour, and reading an enemy host's count from afar trains your scout's Scouting; Off stops both. AI lords still see true numbers. A host's orders in its hover tooltip stay hidden until its count is exact. Off = vanilla counts and orders. Applies immediately. Default: on.

In vanilla, forest makes other parties harder for you to see and slows your party by 20%; it never hides your party from anyone. With this on, your own sight on the campaign map also shrinks by 30% of your base sight while your party travels through forest, and by half that if your scout has the Keen Sight perk. It does not apply inside a settlement. A raised lookout, perks and a Far Watch ride still add to your sight, and the penalties together never take more than half of your base sight. Only your own party is affected; AI parties see as before. The map bar view distance shows the shorter range, but its tooltip has no line for the forest. Off = vanilla sight in forest. Applies immediately. Default: on.

Rebalances who gets a captured town or castle. Off = exact vanilla, where the ruling clan's +60 merit and its unlimited King's Vote override let it take fief after fief. Does not change starting ownership. The ballot's fief count shows either way.

Merit multiplier for the clan that carried the winning assault: the largest share of the winning besieging side's battle contribution, the same number the loot split uses. Every other clan of that kingdom that fielded a party there gets it in proportion, 1 + (bonus - 1) x its share of the top clan's contribution, so a clan with half the top clan's contribution gets half the bonus. Mercenaries and allies from other kingdoms cannot be granted the fief and are not counted. Vanilla's flat +30 for the assault leader's clan is untouched. 1.00 = off. Default: 2.50.

Merit multiplier for a clan that had no party in the winning assault, so land goes to the houses that fought for it. Applies to your clan as well, exempt or not: this is about what a clan did, not what it holds. No effect when nothing is on record for the settlement, such as a fief that changed hands without an assault. 1.00 = off. Default: 0.50.

Merit multiplier for a clan that holds no town or castle at all. Keeps poor clans able to field parties instead of withering and leaving the kingdom. Vanilla already favours landless clans (a flat +30 and nothing in its holdings divisor), so this stacks on a strong base. 1.00 = no bonus. Default: 2.00.

How hard each fief a clan already holds counts against its next claim, as 1/(1 + fiefs x penalty). Vanilla only divides by the VALUE it holds, so a clan sitting on many cheap castles is barely damped. 0.00 = off. Default: 0.35.
Merit multiplier when the clan's culture matches the settlement's. Vanilla has no equivalent, which is how an orc clan ends up holding an elven city. 1.00 = off. Default: 1.50.
Merit multiplier when it does not match. Lower means foreign clans rarely win a settlement of another culture. 1.00 = off. Default: 0.60.
Merit multiplier for the king's own clan, which vanilla already hands a flat +60 on top of its tier and strength. Below 1.00 damps the crown's claim. 1.00 = vanilla. Default: 0.75.

Share of the kingdom's towns and castles above which the ruling clan loses its right to overrule the council. Vanilla lets a king with enough influence override every grant, and his pick is always himself. 1.00 = vanilla. Default: 0.34.

On = your clan keeps every bonus but is never damped for the fiefs it already holds or for a culture mismatch. Off = your clan is scored like any other. Replaces the old Apply Penalties To Your Clan switch, which shipped with the exemption on and let a landed player out-score every AI clan for fiefs they never fought for; the switch was renamed so existing installs pick up the new default. The Absent From Siege Factor applies either way. Default: off.

Lower a dwarf eye height so the third-person camera sits at the head instead of floating above it. Applies to every dwarf, not just the player, so it also moves the aim origin for dwarf troops. Changing this takes effect the next time a dwarf visual is built (opening a character preview, or the next dwarf spawn), not the instant you flip it.

Metres relative to the human eye height. Negative lowers the camera. Default -0.20. The resulting height is clamped to a safe range, so extreme values cannot put the camera in the floor. Like the toggle above, a change lands the next time a dwarf visual is built.

Order resupply convoys from a town, castle or friendly lord: goods from real market stock, troops from volunteers, delivered to you on the map. When off, the order option disappears and no new orders can be placed; convoys already on the road still arrive.
Price multiplier on ordered goods over their market value. Default 1.05.
Delivery fee per map-distance unit between the source and your party. Default 2.
Cost of a mercenary escort per map-distance unit. Default 10.
Guards added to the convoy when a mercenary escort is hired. Default 10.
Convoy travel time per map-distance unit. Default 2. Lower is faster delivery.
Draw the arrow trail from the source to your party while a convoy is on the road. Presentation only.

Pitch camps on the campaign map: field and fortified camps with morale and foraging, terrain-gated ambushes and lookouts. When off, the Make Camp button and camp menus disappear; an existing camp stays until you break it.
Hours to raise a field camp. Ambushes and lookouts take a quarter of this; a fortified camp double. Default 4.
Party morale gained per camped hour once the camp is raised; fortified camps double it. Default 1.
Foraging throughput per troop. Grain per hour also scales with terrain, the party's Scouting skill and the square root of troop count. Default 0.10.
Spotting distance inside which an armed ambush can spring on a passing hostile party. Default 10.
Base chance an eligible passer-by springs the ambush; proximity and Scouting raise it. Default 0.50.
Keep-out radius from towns and castles for pitching a field or fortified camp. 0 disables the check; ambushes and lookouts are exempt. Default 10.
Gold to fortify a raised field camp. Default 500.
Hours a camp work (hunt, fell timber, fish) takes once the men are set to it. Default 10.
Camp Work Yield Per Ten Men
Goods a finished camp work brings in for every ten healthy men, on the best ground for it; poorer ground brings in less. Default 10.
Most goods one finished camp work can bring in, however many men are sent. Default 30.
Camp Rest Healing: Troops Per Day

Extra wounded troops healed per day: a base amount that the usual healing percentages raise too. Works only while the camp panel is open (Camp Options, then Manage camp); the work menus do not count (set both to 0 to turn rest healing off, lodging perks included). Default 15.
Camp Rest Healing: Heroes Per Day

Extra hit points per day for wounded heroes: a base amount that the usual healing percentages raise too. Works only while the camp panel is open (Camp Options, then Manage camp); the work menus do not count (set both to 0 to turn rest healing off, lodging perks included). Default 19.
A new campaign begins with a field camp pitched where the party starts, if the ground allows it; otherwise a message says why and the game goes on as usual. Off by default.

Raise a field or fortified camp into a persistent, garrisonable base. When off: no founding, no upgrading, and your party is not held in place during a build. Standing refuges persist, builds in progress still finish, and refuges can still be entered, managed and dismantled.
Gold to establish a refuge. Default 2000.
Gold to upgrade a refuge into a stronghold. Default 5000.
Hours to raise a refuge after founding; the stronghold rebuild takes the same. Default 6.
Ceiling on simultaneous refuges. The live limit is min(1 + clan tier / 2, this cap). Default 3.
How close your party must be to manage a refuge's garrison and stores. Default 4.
Founding keep-out radius from towns and castles. Default 16.
Stronghold-upgrade keep-out radius from towns and castles. Default 26.
Damage reduction for troops defending a refuge, in battle and in auto-resolve. Default 0.20.
Damage reduction for troops defending a stronghold. Default 0.35.
Base temporary militia rallying to a refuge under attack; age of the refuge and garrison size add more. Default 6.
Ceiling on the temporary defence militia. Default 40.
Experimental: hostile parties can attack your refuges (auto-resolved when you are away). Off by default.
Search radius around a refuge for raid candidates when raids are enabled. Default 6.

Adds a panel to the character creation face generator listing the existing lords of your chosen culture. Pick one and you play the campaign as that lord, with their face, gear, skills, clan, fiefs and kingdom. The character you build is set aside. Off means the panel never loads and character creation is untouched. When the Themed Faction & Hero Picker (Menus & Loading Screens) is shown, it takes this panel's place for that character creation, and a lord picked there is taken over through this feature, so with this off that picker copies the lord's look, gear and skills onto your own character instead.

Also lists the wanderers of your culture. A wanderer has no clan, so instead of taking over a house they are adopted into the clan you named, with the banner you designed, and you lead it. Only 20 of 39 cultures have any wanderers.

Offers the lore-locked dark lords as playable, here and on the Themed Faction & Hero Picker. On by default. The catch: TAOM's capture immunity defers to vanilla for the player character, so a player-controlled Sauron or Witch-king CAN be captured and ransomed like any other lord. Turn this off to keep that lore promise: this list then hides them, and a pick of one on the Themed Faction & Hero Picker only copies his look onto a new character. Saved values from before November 2026 were reset to this default; if you had chosen your own, set it again.

When you take over a lord, adds the starting gold your created character was given on top of the lord's own treasury. An adopted wanderer starts with a new character's gold either way, and an Advanced Start type other than the default sets its own gold. Off by default: an established lord is already funded, so stacking a startup package on them is a balance change rather than a fix.
Kysaro's Middle-earth main menu in place of the vanilla one. Takes effect the next time the main menu opens.
Hides the Bannerlord version number in the corner of the main menu. The TAOM log still records it. Takes effect after a restart: the game builds the version line once, at startup.
Plays the Sauron video behind the main menu in place of the vanilla background video. Takes effect the next time the main menu opens.
Mute Menu Music Under The Video

Keeps the vanilla menu theme off the main menu while the menu video plays its own soundtrack, so it needs Main Menu Video on. Vanilla's music returns once you leave the main menu. Takes effect the next time the main menu opens.
Shows Kysaro's Middle-earth paintings on loading screens, never the same one twice in a row. Only the picture last shown is kept in memory. Takes effect on the next loading screen.

Kysaro's skill icons in place of the vanilla ones, everywhere in the game. Turning them on applies the next time the main menu opens; turning them off takes effect after a restart, because the vanilla icons are not kept once replaced.

Kysaro's faction screen with painted portraits, a map and a hero picker, in place of TAOM's faction map. Picking one of that faction's lords or ladies makes you that character, with their clan, fiefs and kingdom: character creation goes straight to the career choice and then into the game (Player Switcher's settings apply). Picking a legend or any other character starts you with its look, gear and skills. When it is shown it takes the place of Player Switcher's panel for that character creation. Takes effect the next time character creation reaches the culture screen.
Kysaro's reskin of the character creation face generator. Outside character creation the face generator stays vanilla. Takes effect the next time it opens.
Kysaro's reskin of the family, childhood, adolescence, youth, adulthood and age screens. Takes effect the next time one of them opens.
Kysaro's reskin of the final review screen, where you name your character. Takes effect the next time it opens.
The themed, layered banner editor, both during character creation and in a running campaign. Takes effect the next time it opens.
Kysaro's reskin of the clan naming screen. Takes effect the next time it opens.
Kysaro's reskin of the difficulty and campaign options screen at the end of character creation. Takes effect the next time it opens.

Spawns a 10-30 minute background task that recomputes the settlement distance cache against the live map scene. Requires an active campaign. Game stays playable but pathfinding queries during the rebuild may be inconsistent — best run from main menu after loading a save.

Whether spider broods keep spawning around Mirkwood and Dol Guldur on the campaign map (one a day, up to twenty). Off stops new broods; broods already on the map stay. Broods exist only in a campaign started with v2.0.32 or later.

Whether wild troll bands keep spawning on the campaign map, about one per kingdom near its towns, castles and villages (one new band a day, two to four trolls each). Trolls are never taken prisoner or recruited. Off stops new bands; bands already on the map stay. Troll bands need a new campaign. The options below tune the spiders only.
Hit points of a riderless creature bandit (the giant spiders of the Mirkwood broods). The ridden spider mount keeps its own. Applies to creatures spawned after the change.
How many soldiers the standing front bite can strike at once (the nearest ones in its arc).
How many soldiers the running pounce can strike at once.
How many soldiers a left or right swipe can strike at once.
Bite damage as a percentage of the spider's base bite (100 = the ridden spider's damage).
Pounce damage as a percentage of the spider's base bite.
Swipe damage as a percentage of the spider's base bite. Low by default: the swipe reaches several soldiers.
When on, a creature's normal hit only staggers a soldier and only a critical hit knocks him down. When off, any hit of 30 or more knocks down, as the ridden spider's do.
Seconds between a creature's pounces or bites. Applies to creatures spawned after the change.
Seconds between a creature's swipes. Applies to creatures spawned after the change.
Share of damage a creature takes from arrows, bolts, javelins and thrown weapons (100 = normal). Applies at once.
Share of damage a creature takes from cutting melee blows: swords, axes (100 = normal).
Share of damage a creature takes from piercing melee blows: spears, thrusts (100 = normal).
Share of damage a creature takes from blunt melee blows: maces, hammers, charges (100 = normal).

Draws each kingdom's border on the campaign map, following rivers, coasts and mountain ranges, and redraws it when a fief changes hands. While this is on, the Show Realm Borders key (M by default) hides and shows them, and the map mode key (G) switches what they show.
Heraldic Bands Instead of Atlas Look
Off: the Atlas look, a watercolour wash inside each border with a dash-dot ink line. On: two solid bands in each realm's colour with a gap on the line.
Draws your own kingdom's frontier as a gold cord, so you can find it at a glance.
Multiplies the width of every border. Default: 1.
Camera distance at which the borders start to appear; closer than this they are hidden. Must be below Full Opacity Distance, or both revert to their defaults. Default: 45.
Camera distance at which the borders are fully drawn. Default: 110.
On: borders always show, drawn over hills and map figures. Off: borders lie on the ground and hide behind ridges.
Letters each kingdom's name across its land when the camera is zoomed out.
Tells you when your party rides into another kingdom's lands.
Tints each kingdom's land in its colour between the borders, like a map in an atlas.
How strongly the land is tinted: 0.05 is a faint wash, 0.8 nearly paints over the map. Default: 0.5.
As you zoom all the way out, a parchment map of Middle-earth fades in over the campaign map, with the borders, realm colours and names drawn on it. It shows only while the borders do.

Advanced: how the borders mix with the map beneath. 'Material default' keeps the engine material's own. If the borders glow and their dark ink line is missing, try Modulate (Factor turns blending off).

Advanced: the engine material the borders are drawn from. 'Automatic' tries vertex_color_blend_after_postfx_mat first, which blends normally so the dark ink line shows, then the others in list order. Every choice draws over the parchment map.

Rhudaur's colour on the map, written #RRGGBB. Blank uses the default, #E0735A.
Ered Luin's colour on the map, written #RRGGBB. Blank uses the default, #7B68EE.
Anduin Vale's colour on the map, written #RRGGBB. Blank uses the default, #654D37.
Angáladh's colour on the map, written #RRGGBB. Blank uses the default, #587A4A.
Dorwinion's colour on the map, written #RRGGBB. Blank uses the default, #722721.
South Rhovanion's colour on the map, written #RRGGBB. Blank uses the default, #4B3F0F.

The colour of your realm when it is none of the kingdoms above: your clan's land while it serves no kingdom, then a kingdom you found. Written #RRGGBB. Blank gives it a free colour. In one of the kingdoms above, that kingdom's own field applies.

Orc and goblin warriors in a battle line no longer walk in lockstep: each soldier's step size is scaled by a random factor between the minimum below and 1.0, fixed for that soldier. Applied when a soldier spawns, so it takes effect in the next battle.

Each soldier's step size is vanilla's step size times a random factor between this value and 1.00. Vanilla's own step size is 0.80 at Athletics 0 and rises to 1.00 at Athletics 300, so the factor is not the final step size: at 0.92 an Athletics 0 soldier ends at 0.74 to 0.80 and an Athletics 300 soldier at 0.92 to 1.00, and at 0.80 the lowest step size is 0.64. 1.00 turns the spread off. A value outside 0.80 to 1.00 falls back to 0.92.

Each orc and goblin warrior walks with one of several gait sets, picked at random and fixed for that soldier. A gait set that is not installed is skipped, so with none installed this does nothing. Applied when a soldier spawns, so it takes effect in the next battle.

Tests alternative swing clips: when a mission has act_taom_ swing codes loaded, it counts which clip each swing plays and where in the clip a hit lands, and only logs; it changes nothing in the game. While such codes exist it costs a per-frame sweep of every person in every mission, towns included; with none loaded it writes one log line per mission. Read at the start of each mission.

When enabled (default), a castle or town whose realm is at war with yours harasses a lord party that marches within a few map units of its walls, if the fort is not besieged and holds enough troops (30 by default). Your party is slowed (disorganized: it moves slower, and its troops start a battle with lower morale until it wears off) and loses a few men, some food and morale. An army you lead loses cohesion, but never below 10, and each party marching with you takes its own losses. When off, forts never harass anyone. Applies at once, no restart.

When enabled (default), AI lords marching past an enemy fort are slowed (disorganized) too, at a lower chance than yours, and lose nothing else. Turn it off to protect the campaign pace: the effect then stays on your own party and the army you lead (AI lords marching with your army still take their share). Does nothing while Enable Watchful Holds is off.

When enabled (default), raiding hosts ride once the War of the Ring is in Full War, or from day 89 when the War of the Ring is switched off. They ride out of their homelands to burn the villages of the opposed side: Orcs of Gundabad, Easterlings of Rhûn, Haradrim, Dunlendings and the Blacklocks of Erebor against the Free Peoples; outlaw bands of Gondor and Mirkwood against the Shadow; Corsairs of Umbar against either. A host raids the villages of the strongest enemy realm, fights weaker parties of that realm it meets, and goes home after its quota. When off, no host rides and a host already out is sent away at its next hourly tick; one still fighting is sent away once its battle ends. Single player only. Applies at once, no restart.
When enabled (default), the outlaw bands of Gondor and Mirkwood may ride against the Shadow's realms. Does nothing while Enable Fire and Tribute is off.
When enabled (default), the Corsair Host of Umbar may ride against Free or Shadow realms. Does nothing while Enable Fire and Tribute is off.
When enabled (default), the hosts of Gundabad, Rhûn, Harad and Dunland, and the Blacklocks of Erebor, may ride against the Free Peoples' realms. Does nothing while Enable Fire and Tribute is off.

When enabled (default), a host that rides against your kingdom sends an envoy a day or two later, if your clan owns villages and you are not enlisted. The envoy asks for gold, at a price that grows with your villages and with each envoy you have seized. Pay and the host raids none of your clan's villages and never attacks your party; haggle once (a Charm roll) when the tribute is large; ask for time; refuse; or seize the envoy, after which that side's next host rides against your kingdom first. Shown only while the map is free. When off, no envoy is scheduled or shown. Single player only. Applies at once, no restart.

When enabled (default), an AI lord stops running from an army that besieges a settlement when the lord, with its army if it leads one or is attached to it, is at least half as strong as the entire siege camp (0.5 by default, unlooked_for_aid.json). Lords can then pass a siege or gather near it. A lord shut inside a besieged settlement is never fled from, whatever the strengths. A weaker lord still flees, so it is not caught when the siege lifts beside it. At a siege you lead, AI lords keep the base game behaviour. Caravans, villagers, bandits, patrols and garrisons are unchanged. When off, lords flee exactly as in the base game. Applies at once, no restart.

When enabled (default), the Army Management screen works during a siege you lead as the besieger: you can call parties into your army and release them while the siege goes on, at the usual influence cost. The base game's other limits still apply (a party that is fighting, too weak, disbanding, too far away or at sea is refused, and so is a party already at the siege outside your army). Defending a siege, having no army and being in a map event keep the base game block. Singleplayer only: in a co-op session this does nothing. When off, the block is exactly the base game's. Takes effect the next time the screen opens, no restart.
Rulers call hosts for less influence

When enabled (default), an AI kingdom ruler, Good or Evil, pays half the influence (0.5 by default, RulerCallCostFactor in army_targeting.json) for each party called into an army, after culture feats. Cheaper calls also make the influence an army spends on keeping itself together cheaper for the ruler, so those hosts hold longer and the ruler's clan keeps more influence for votes. Your own calls, as a ruler or a vassal, cost what they always did. Singleplayer only: in a co-op session this does nothing. When off, the ruler pays the usual cost; culture feats and the Realms liege army discount still apply. The two discounts do not stack: when both apply to a call, the larger one is used. Applies at once, no restart.

Relation with lords and notables is earned on campaign: fighting beside a lord, clearing bandits near a settlement, handing a lord troops, and overpaying in a barter. Off restores vanilla on all four. Does nothing while you are enlisted. Default: on.

Relation gained with each lord who fought on your side in a battle, once per lord per battle (once per clan when Personal Relations is off, because a clan then shares one relation). Your own clan, an army you lead and lords leading no party earn nothing; after a win, the side leader you came to help is thanked by vanilla's own conversation instead, but only when vanilla pays him something (a small contribution earns him this bonus). 0 = none. Default: 1.

Each lord who fought against you in a battle thinks less of you, once per lord per battle (once per clan when Personal Relations is off, because a clan then shares one relation). Bandits are never counted. Default: off.
How much relation each enemy lord loses when the option above is on. 0 = none. Default: 5.
Notables Thank You For Clearing Bandits

In the field, against bandits alone (cleared hideouts are thanked by vanilla): after you win, one random notable in each settlement near the battle gains relation with you, one point for every ten bandits killed, wounded or routed, at least 1 and at most 10. A village in the other side's land (Free against Evil) does not thank you. Default: on.
How far from the battle, in map units, a settlement still thanks you. A settlement is usually about 17 units from its nearest neighbour. Default: 25.

When you hand troops to another lord on the Donate Troops screen, that lord gains relation with you: half of the influence the gift is worth, at most 10, give or take one. A gift worth less than 2 earns nothing. Hand-overs stop paying a lord once 10 relation has landed with him that day; the Done that reaches 10 asks only for what is left, and Charm can raise it. A lord gains at most 10 a day from hand-overs, however the gift is split (Charm can raise the last Done). The same rule pays for troops given to a lord through a Lord Courtesies gift. Default: on.
Most Relation From One Barter Overpay

The most relation one barter can buy by offering more than the goods are worth. The loop buys at most 3 points in vanilla (the setting here), before the Tribute perk (x1.2, rounded up) and the Charm relation bonus the engine adds when it applies the change. Points cost more the further relation is from 0, so only a large overpay reaches the cap. Default: 15.

Your relation with a lord stays with that lord instead of passing to his clan leader, so a friendship with Faramir is not a friendship with Denethor. Affects only your own relations: relations between AI lords stay vanilla. Single player only: in a co-op session or on a dedicated server it stays vanilla. A save made before this was on is seeded once: on the first day this is on, each living lord whose personal relation with you is 0 takes his clan leader's value, and it is seeded again when this has been off for at least one in-game day. Off restores vanilla. Default: on.

Paying influence to disband another lord's army costs you relation with the army's leader by the amounts below (vanilla is 4); each other lord in it costs vanilla's 1. Applies only in single player, and only while Enable Personal Relations is on. Default: on.

The least relation you lose with an army's leader when you pay influence to disband it. The cost is a random whole number between the least and the most. If the least is above the most, the two swap. Applies only in single player, and only while Enable Personal Relations is on. Default: 28.
The most relation you lose with an army's leader when you pay influence to disband it. Applies only in single player, and only while Enable Personal Relations is on. Default: 32.

A routing enemy soldier who has just been hit, with a few of your men right beside him and enough health left, turns and fights instead of running on, and routers close to him turn with him (a few at most). They keep fighting only while one of your men is still near them and some of their side still stand; once the whole side has broken they run again, so the battle still ends in a rout. Soldiers of cultures that never rout, and soldiers ordered to retreat, are not touched. Field battles, sieges and sally-outs. Default: on.
A routing soldier turns to fight only while this many of your men or fewer are within a few steps of him. Default: 3.

Enemy archers that have nothing to shoot at, are steady, and are within bow range of you may fix on you and shoot, for a few seconds at a time. A cap keeps the volley small. Archers of a team that is making a stand against horse are left to that stand. Field battles, sieges and sally-outs. Default: on.
The chance each second that an idle archer in range fixes on you. 0 never, 1 always. Default: 0.25.
The most enemy archers that hold you as their target at the same moment. Default: 8.

In a large field battle, when only a few enemy soldiers are left, none of them a hero and none still to arrive, the survivors are sent off the field after a pause so the battle ends in your win and they can be taken prisoner. Sieges and sally-outs are not changed. Default: on.
The cleanup starts when this many enemy soldiers or fewer are left. Default: 3.
Seconds the battle must stay down to the last few before the survivors are sent off, one a second. Default: 30.
Writes a [FellFoes] line each second something is stopped, held or sent off, and whether held archers really are aiming at you. For checking the feature; leave off in normal play. Default: off.

Adds "I have a gift for you." to the talk with the companions in your party and, on the diplomacy branch, with lords who are not children, not prisoners, not in your own clan and not at war with you. Goods the catalog lists, from your inventory, win relation; companions also take gold purses. A co-op client, or a peer running a co-op mod TAOM cannot probe, sees no gift line. Default: on.
Days Between Gifts To One Hero

After a gift, the same hero takes no other for this many days, so goods cannot be turned straight into relation. Whenever Personal Relations is not engaged (switched off, a co-op host, or a save not yet seeded) a clan shares one relation, so the days count for the whole clan. The count is saved with the campaign. Default: 7.
Most Relation One Gift Asks For

The most relation one gift asks for, after the taste bonus and the scaling by relation (above relation 0 a gift adds (90 minus relation) / 90 of its worth, so a 1-point gift stops working near relation 45 and nothing helps at 90). A companion's gift starts at 1 to 5 by the item's value; a lord's starts at the catalog's value for the goods (1 to 10), and a hero who prizes the goods adds a bonus. Your Charm can add to what lands. Default: 15.
Free Lords Refuse Gifts From Evil Players
A lord of a Free realm will not take a gift from a player who sides with the Shadow. The lord refuses with no penalty. Realms and cultures that side with neither never refuse. Default: on.

The gold in the smallest purse you can give a companion. The gold leaves you and goes to the companion. A purse is worth 1 relation per 500 gold, at most 10 (5000 gold), before the scaling and the cap. Between 500 and 5000 gold. Default: 500.
The gold in the middle purse you can give a companion. A purse is worth 1 relation per 500 gold, at most 10 (5000 gold). Between 500 and 5000 gold. Default: 2000.
The gold in the largest purse you can give a companion. A purse is worth 1 relation per 500 gold, at most 10 (5000 gold). Between 500 and 5000 gold. Default: 5000.

Counts soldiers, mounts and creatures that are stuck in a battle, standing off the walkable ground or wading in water without moving, and writes what it finds to the log with a [LostFooting] tag, with a summary when the battle ends. It only watches: it never moves or changes anything in the battle. With the rescue on, the start line and the summary are still written. Field battles, sieges and sally-outs. Default: on.

Moves a soldier who stays stuck back to where he can walk: off the walkable ground or still in water for 10 seconds, he steps to the nearest good spot within 6 m at his own height; still stuck after 30 seconds, he moves to his place in his formation while you are at least 25 m away. A riderless horse gets the short step only. Never the player, fleeing men, creatures, men working a ladder or machine, or men holding a set post or waiting at a ladder. Field battles, sieges and sally-outs, not co-op. Default: on.

Turns the three rewards on or off together: relation for releasing a captured lord, for donating a hero prisoner to a settlement and for winning a town's tournament. Each reward also has its own switch below. Applies on the host in co-op. Default: on.

Releasing a captured lord from your party (in conversation or on the party screen) or from your own dungeon earns relation with the lord, with the lord's living spouse and with the lord's clan leader. The post-battle "free to go" choice, ransom, peace, escape and any AI release earn nothing. Default: on.
Handing a hero prisoner to a settlement adds a bonus to the relation vanilla gives with the settlement owner's clan leader. Default: on.
Winning a town's tournament earns relation with the owner's clan leader (unless your clan owns the town) and with every notable in the town. Default: on.
Relation asked for with the lord you release, before the alignment multiplier. Vanilla pays another 4 in the conversation. Your Charm can add to what lands. Default: 5.
Release: Relation With The Lord's Spouse
Relation asked for with the lord's living spouse, before the alignment multiplier. Default: 2.
Release: Relation With The Lord's Clan Leader

Relation asked for with the leader of the lord's clan, before the alignment multiplier. While Personal Relations is off, the lord and the clan leader share one relation, so only the larger of the two is paid. Default: 2.

Relation added to what vanilla gives with the settlement owner's clan leader for each hero prisoner donated, before the alignment multiplier. Vanilla itself pays nothing when the captive likes the owner. Default: 5.
Relation asked for with the town owner's clan leader and with each notable in the town when you win its tournament, before the alignment multiplier. Between 0 and 10. Default: 1.
Multiplier on every release reward when you and the lord are on the same side (both Free, or both Shadow). Results round half away from zero, and 0 grants nothing. Default: 1.00.
Multiplier on every release reward when you or the lord is on neither side. Default: 0.75.
Multiplier on every release reward when you and the lord are on opposite sides, so freeing an enemy of your cause earns little. Default: 0.50.

Multiplier on the donation relation when the captive and the settlement owner are on the same side. Zero means no reward, and no vanilla relation either, for jailing a friend of the owner. Default: 0.00.
Multiplier on the donation relation when the captive or the settlement owner is on neither side. Default: 1.00.
Multiplier on the donation relation (vanilla's gain plus the bonus) when the captive is on the opposite side to the settlement owner, such as a Mordor captive handed to Minas Tirith. Default: 2.00.
Multiplier on the tournament relation with an owner or notable on your side. Default: 1.00.
Multiplier on the tournament relation with an owner or notable who, or whose realm, is on neither side. Default: 1.00.
Multiplier on the tournament relation with an owner or notable on the opposite side, who does not cheer a champion of the other cause. Default: 0.00.

Turns on the extra relation loss, on top of vanilla's own, that a village's owner and notables hold against you when you raid the village or force it to give goods or recruits. Villages your clan owns are never affected, and neither are raids you do not lead. Applies on the host in co-op. Default: on.
A raid you lead costs relation with the owner's clan leader and with every notable of the village, in proportion to the damage the raid did. A raid that did none costs nothing. Default: on.

Forcing a village to give goods or recruits costs relation with the owner's clan leader and with every notable, whether the villagers resist or give way. A resisting village that wins the fight costs nothing. Default: on.
Raid: Relation Lost With The Owner's Clan Leader
Relation lost with the clan leader who owns the village after a whole raid, before the alignment multiplier. Vanilla takes its own share as well. Between 0 and 100. Default: 50.
Raid: Relation Lost With Each Notable
Relation lost with every notable of the village after a whole raid, before the alignment multiplier. Vanilla takes its own share as well. Between 0 and 100. Default: 50.
Forced Taking: Relation Lost With The Owner's Clan Leader
Relation lost with the clan leader who owns the village each time you force it to give goods or recruits, before the alignment multiplier. Between 0 and 50. Default: 20.
Forced Taking: Relation Lost With Each Notable
Relation lost with every notable of the village each time you force it to give goods or recruits, before the alignment multiplier. Between 0 and 50. Default: 25.
Multiplier on the loss when you and the village owner's realm are on the same side, both Free or both Evil: the harshest pairing. Default: 1.00.
Multiplier on the loss when you or the village owner's realm is on neither side. Default: 0.50.
Multiplier on the loss when you and the village owner's realm are on opposite sides, such as an Evil warband raiding a Free village, where raiding is expected. Default: 0.10.

On the Members tab of the clan screen, gives the row of a companion of your clan a faint red tint when their relation with you has fallen below zero, a warning before they leave. The age beside each child's name is always shown. Applies the next time the clan screen opens. Default: on.

On the party screen, a captive lord's row shows the clan's banner at the top left of the portrait, the kingdom's banner at the top right (when the clan belongs to a kingdom), and a gold noble icon at the bottom left when the lord leads the clan. Applies the next time the party screen opens. Default: on.

In the dungeon menu of a town or castle, adds under the engine's own line how many prisoners the dungeon holds against its capacity, how many of them are lords, each lord's chance to escape each day with the terms behind it (your clan holding him halves it; the governor's perks change it), and a line for a lord whose realm has a War of the Ring escape boost, or whom nothing lets escape. It only shows the odds the game already uses and changes no rule. Applies the next time the menu opens. Default: on.

When enabled (default), a captured lord can be asked to join your kingdom, in a conversation or from the party screen, and serves it instead of being ransomed. The lord must hold a clan of another kingdom (not its ruler, and not a mercenary or minor clan), must be held by your party or in a settlement your clan owns, and must not be a lord who can never be captured, such as Sauron and the Nazgul. A Free Peoples lord is never asked to join an Evil realm, and an Evil lord is never asked to join a Free one. The base game's blood feud rule still applies. When off, the base game's rules apply: only a kingdom's ruler can recruit a captured lord, through its 'join us, and be set free' line, which checks no realm. When on, both lines pass this check, and the ruler-only line also needs the lord held by your party or in your clan's dungeon. Applies at once, no restart.

Lets the hero you name Quartermaster (never you, and only while that hero is in your party) take standing orders in conversation: buy food at markets, slaughter livestock when the stores run low, lift the host's spirits with pay or drink, and sell your goods at a nearby town for a cut. Orders stand down for an enlisted player and for a co-op client. Default: on.

When the food in the stores, not counting the herd, lasts fewer days than this, the slaughter order turns livestock into meat, a head at a time, until it lasts this long again. Between 1 and 30. Default: 3.
The slaughter order always leaves this many head of each livestock type alive. The game itself still slaughters livestock when every other food is gone. Between 0 and 20. Default: 2.
Gold paid to each soldier (not you) by the small pay option, in a settlement or a ready field camp. Between 10 and 500. Default: 50.
Morale the party gains from the small pay option. Between 1 and 30. Default: 5.
Gold paid to each soldier (not you) by the large pay option. Never read below the small pay's gold. Between 10 and 500. Default: 100.
Morale the party gains from the large pay option. Never read below the small pay's morale. Between 1 and 30. Default: 10.

The food order never spends the gold your party needs for this many days of wages, so buying food cannot leave your troops unpaid. 0 lets it spend the whole purse. Morale purchases are not limited: they show their price. Between 0 and 30. Default: 3.

The Provender-master's cut, in percent of a town's price, when you send goods to be sold there and the Provender-master has no Trade skill. It falls to the smallest cut at Trade 250, and each town further down the list adds 5. Between 0 and 90. Default: 30.
The Provender-master's cut at Trade 250. Never read above the largest cut. Between 0 and 90. Default: 10.

How many of the nearest towns that will buy from you the Provender-master offers. A town at war with you, of the opposing alignment, besieged, barring you or short of gold is never offered. Between 1 and 5. Default: 3.

The fewest days a clan that signs on as a mercenary stays with its kingdom. Until then it cannot leave a ruler who is in debt, be hired away by another kingdom, or leave in its daily consideration of whether to stay. A clan with more time left is not shortened. Your own clan is not bound, and neither is dismissing or hiring away a mercenary yourself. 0 turns it off. Applies when a clan signs on; clans already serving get it at their next signing. Between 0 and 120. Default: 30.
These mercenaries would desert your party: their people will not serve your side.
Fight for your side? No coin buys that. Find your swords elsewhere.

Your swings with a two-handed axe, mace, sword or polearm can cut through one enemy and strike the next. Each enemy after the first takes less damage. Armour slows the blade, and a kill or a clear skill lead over the victim carries it further. Cleaving Blows never applies to a shield block, a thrust or a swing from horseback. Only the character you control, unless the AI option below is on. Trolls and other big creatures keep their own cleave. The numbers live in combat_mechanics_config.json. Default: on.

AI soldiers who swing a two-handed axe, mace or sword cut through enemies by the same rules. Every two-handed troop in both armies then hits a packed line harder. Needs Cleaving Blows on. Default: off.
The most enemies one swing can strike, the first one included. Default 3. A swing often stops sooner: each enemy takes some of its force, and armour takes more.
The saved game failed to load
An error occurred while this save loaded, and the game cannot continue the load. The error is in the TAOM log. Quit the game, then send that log with a bug report.
Pause the input method outside text fields

For Chinese, Japanese and Korean input methods. While the game is in front and no text field has focus, the input method is paused, so hotkeys on the map and in battle reach the game instead of opening its candidate window. A search, rename or other text field gets it back at once, and other programs are not affected. Applies immediately. Default: on.

Experimental. In field battles, sieges and the Fords of War match soldiers have stamina. A melee swing, a shot, a throw, a jump, a kick, a shield bash and a blow stopped with a weapon or shield cost stamina, and running on foot drains it down to half. Stamina comes back while a soldier does not attack, more slowly while a block is held and not at all while running. A tired soldier swings and handles a weapon more slowly, and a tired AI soldier attacks less often. A soldier whose stamina reaches zero is exhausted until it is back at about a third: an exhausted soldier cannot attack, block, kick or jump, and on foot slows to a walk. Exceptions: a soldier who works a siege engine pays nothing and is not stopped, and a rider or a swimmer can still jump. Higher tier troops and heroes have more stamina. A soldier's people changes it too: Elves, Dwarves, Uruk-hai and trolls have more than most Men of the same rank, Orcs and goblins have less, and the Nazgul do not tire. Horses and other mounts are not affected. Takes effect from the next battle. Default: off.
You are tiring. Ease off before your strength fails.
Your strength fails you. Fall back and catch your breath.

Multiplies what every action costs in stamina, for every soldier: the player, allies and enemies alike. 0.50 halves the costs, 2.00 doubles them. It does not change how fast stamina comes back or how much a soldier has. Read at each battle tick. Default: 1.00.

Shows your own stamina as a bar beside the battle HUD rings while Combat Stamina is on. The bar changes colour as you tire and turns grey while you are exhausted. Off hides the bar only: stamina still works. Drawn on this client only. Default: on.

When on, the soldier you control has stamina while Combat Stamina is on: your actions cost it and you can become exhausted. Off exempts that soldier: your stamina never drains, you are never stopped, and the stamina bar is hidden. AI soldiers still follow the next setting. Read at each battle tick. Default: on.

When on, the soldiers the AI controls have stamina while Combat Stamina is on, allies and enemies alike. Off exempts them all: only the soldier you control tires, if the setting above is on. Read at each battle tick. Default: on.
